label: first copy step (recall_idx 1) re-inputting an initial s, in sequences starting s/x/f-heavy
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.005% of steps). 95% of activation mass is in the copy phase, 88% at recall_idx 1 (step L+1, where the model feeds back its first output orig(0)); in_tok is s for 82% of mass (r is a distant second at 9%). Within those steps it is selective for sequences whose first few original tokens come from {s, x, f} (e.g. s s x..., s f x..., s x x...); the strongest activations (top ~0.2) are all s followed by s/f/x then x. It favours longer sequences (L 7-9) and is almost silent in the original phase and at the delimiter, except for rare weak firings. It does NOT fire on most s inputs at step L+1: (recall_idx==1 & in_tok==s) has recall 0.74 but precision only 1.4%. Requiring orig(1) and orig(2) in {s,x,f} raises precision to ~0.40, but recall drops to ~0.22 (dev F1 0.29). So the precise conjunction of prefix tokens that drives it is not captured. Magnitude is higher when orig(1)/orig(2) are x/s/f (top quartile coverage 0.66 vs 0.33 for the lowest quartile).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=s (+4.13), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=r (+3.58), phase=2 & out_tok=r (+2.84), orig1=s (+2.72), orig1=x (+2.49), orig0=s (+2.43). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-1.78), orig2=g (-1.46), orig8=- (-0.97), to_go=3 (-0.83).
